newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up on follow-up buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up on follow-up buying.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up for the fourth day in a row on Thursday on active follow-up buying despite a correction in the afternoon in line with the A share market, brokers said.
The B share index rose 0.332 points or 0.46 percent to 73.273 points on volume of 23.1 million shares worth $11.1 million compared with $10.7 million on Wednesday.
The A share index reversed the morning gains to end down at 1,271.612 points, falling 1.277 points or 0.10 percent on turnover of 10.6 billion yuan.
Brokers said active domestic buying firmly supported the B share market, though overseas investors remained mainly on the sidelines with 1996 annual results of most firms unclear.
"The market is small, so domestic buying easily boosted the index," one broker said.
"The index will continue to rise in the short term if domestic A shares can hold the current bullish trend," a second broker said. "But it is likely to meet resistance at about 75 points."
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded with 21 up, seven flat and 13 down.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the star on talk of financial reconstructuring, brokers said.
It jumped $0.112 or 10 percent to limit-up of $1.234 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device traded the most on inter-institutional trading, ending flat at $0.23 on volume of 2.5 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index reversed early gains on a technical correction, but market tone remained good with trading active, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue chip index slipped 74.51 points or 2.13 percent to 3,418.969 points.
Fuzhou Dongjiekou Department Store was the biggest winner on speculative buying, soaring 0.99 yuan to limit-up of 10.87 yuan on volume of seven million shares.
